column1: # mutation-exclusions.tsv — in-universe guards the sweep does NOT mutate.
# The guard universe is a RULE, not a list: every git-tracked `*.sh` that is not a
# `*-selftest.sh` and is not under `*/evals/*` or `tests/hooks-smoke/`. Every guard in that
# universe must resolve to its killer(s) via directory-scoped same-stem pairing, a
# `mutation-pair-map.tsv` row, or a row here. An unaccounted guard is RED — that is what
# keeps this file honest as the tree grows.
# RESOLUTION SEMANTICS: a row here PREEMPTS pairing entirely. An excluded guard that also
# carries pair-map rows is a lint error, not a silent precedence win.
# Two of these restate exceptions CLAUDE.md's "Genuine exceptions" register already
# carries. Those rows CITE that register as their origin rather than asserting an
# independent rationale — one register stays authoritative and this one defers to it, so
# the two cannot drift into disagreeing. Dropping an entry there obliges dropping it here.

column2: CLAUDE.md "Genuine exceptions" register — by design, no independent contract (shared registry mechanics). No independent contract means no kill criterion, so a mutant here has nothing to survive against. Origin: CLAUDE.md, not this file.

CLAUDE.md "Genuine exceptions" register — the documented deliberate coverage exception (bootstraps the bot wrapper from a private key; no selftest can exercise it without minting credentials). Origin: CLAUDE.md, not this file.

Local operator tooling with no CI contract — never invoked by any workflow or gate. NOTE: it shares a stem with plugins/second-shift/templates/consumer/second-shift-doctor.sh, which IS swept via its own directory-scoped same-stem suite. The two are separate files with no lockstep row pairing them, so this exclusion covers only the .claude/tools/ copy; basename-anywhere matching would have swept operator tooling against the template's foreign suite, which is why same-stem resolution is directory-scoped.

The harness never sweeps itself — recursion guard. Its same-stem pair with tools/mutation-sweep-selftest.sh is real and the companion suite does exercise it; this row suppresses only the self-sweep, not the coverage.
